notes: Reading B, as latitude. SR6a asks that the object's operands be "valid operands for comparison to the corresponding operand" of the subject: a property of the operand PAIR (class, usage, index rules of VI.6.3.1.1.1-3), not of a relation condition as a whole; "must contain at least one reference to a variable" is a sentence about "the relation condition", and EVALUATE builds no relation condition: GR1b assigns a literal subject and a literal object the value and class of the literal alike and GR2a compares the values "according to the rules for comparison". The page reference in SR6a ("See page VI-54") lands on the page holding the variable sentence, so reading A survives the words, hence latitude. ISO does not govern the 1985 question (and its answer is neither reading: Table 15, §2023:14.9.13.3 SR10, blanks literal x literal but permits literal x range and arithmetic-expression x literal). GnuCOBOL 3.2 with -std=cobol85 compiles and runs EVALUATE ZERO WHEN 0, EVALUATE 5 WHEN 5, EVALUATE "A" WHEN "A", EVALUATE 5 WHEN NOT 4 and IF 0 = 0 (all HIT), i.e. B. The compiler matches neither 1985 reading: its COBOL1634 refusal is the 2023 Table 15 cell (the message cites §2023:14.9.13.3 SR10 Table 15), applied at --std 85 with no edition gate; at 85 it refuses EVALUATE ZERO WHEN 0, 5 WHEN 5, "A" WHEN "A", 5 WHEN NOT 4 and 5 ALSO N3 WHEN 5 ALSO 12, and accepts 5 WHEN 1 THRU 9, "A" WHEN "A" THRU "Z", 1 + 1 WHEN 2, 12 WHEN N3. Under B the refusals reject legal source (the defect); under A the accepted no-variable pairings would be the defect instead, and the compiler's own IF 0 = 0 at --std 85 is only warning COBOL3146, so A is not how the compiler treats the relation condition either. Every other pairing the read probed conforms to SR6a/SR6b. PARTIAL, rejects legal source. kb/Work PB5481 holds the defect (adjudication: held-85/set8/decisions.json (the adjudication of coderead-85/held-9.json, the 1985 read 4)).

next.reason: §2023:14.9.13.3 SR7 a-c restate 1985 a-c: objects 'shall be valid operands for comparison', condition-2, TRUE or FALSE 'shall correspond to condition-1 or the words TRUE or FALSE', and 'ANY may correspond to a selection subject of any type'. §2023:14.9.13.3 SR10 (Table 15) states the same pairings; its blank literal/literal cell matches the 1985 relation-condition rule 'must contain at least one reference to a variable'. But SR7 widens a) from 'arithmetic expressions' to 'expressions' (boolean too), and its d) admits partial-expression-1 for identifier, literal, arithmetic or boolean subjects. 1985 refuses an object such as '> 5', which 2023 accepts. Compile-time rules both.
